questions.text:
Consider the following expression grammar G:
E[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]E-T|T
T[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]T+F|F
F[latex]\rightarrow[/latex](E)|id
Which of the following grammars is not left recursive, but is equivalent to G?
questions.solution:
Remove left recursion with the standard rule [latex]A\rightarrow A\alpha\mid\beta\Rightarrow A\rightarrow\beta A',\ A'\rightarrow\alpha A'\mid\epsilon[/latex]:
- [latex]E\rightarrow E-T\mid T[/latex] becomes [latex]E\rightarrow TX,\ X\rightarrow-TX\mid\epsilon[/latex]
- [latex]T\rightarrow T+F\mid F[/latex] becomes [latex]T\rightarrow FY,\ Y\rightarrow+FY\mid\epsilon[/latex]

Option 1 is still left recursive, option 2 keeps [latex]T\rightarrow T+F[/latex] and loses the minus, option 4 changes the language.

Answer: Option 3

questions.text: The minimum possible number of states of a deterministic automaton that accepts the regular language [latex]L=\{w_{1}aw_{2}|w_{1},w_{2}\in \{a,b\}^{*},|w_{1}|=2,|w_{2}|\geq 3\}[/latex] is ____
questions.solution:
The DFA has to:
- read the 2 symbols of [latex]w_1[/latex]: states q0, q1, q2
- check that the 3rd symbol is a: q3 (a b here goes to a dead state)
- count at least 3 symbols of [latex]w_2[/latex]: q4, q5, then q6, which is accepting and loops on a, b
- plus the dead state

Total = 7 + 1 = 8 states, all distinguishable.

Answer: 8

questions.text:
Identify the language generated by the following grammar, where S is start variable.
S[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] XY
X[latex]\rightarrow[/latex] aX|a
Y [latex]\rightarrow[/latex]aYb|[latex]\in[/latex]
questions.solution:
X gives [latex]a^k[/latex] with k [latex]\ge[/latex] 1; Y gives [latex]a^nb^n[/latex] with n [latex]\ge[/latex] 0. Together: [latex]a^{k+n}b^n[/latex], so the a's are strictly more than the b's.

Answer: [latex]\{a^mb^n\mid m \gt n,\ n\ge0\}[/latex]

questions.text:
Which of the following statements about parser is/are CORRECT?
I. Canonical LR is more powerful than SLR.
II. SLR is more powerful than LALR
III. SLR is more powerful than Canonical LR.
questions.solution:
Power of LR parsers: LR(0) [latex]\lt[/latex] SLR [latex]\lt[/latex] LALR [latex]\lt[/latex] Canonical LR. So only "Canonical LR is more powerful than SLR" is correct.

Answer: I only

questions.text:
Let [latex]L_{1},L_{2}[/latex] be any two context free languages and R be any regular language. Then which of the following is/are CORRECT ?
I. [latex]L_{1}\cup L_{2}[/latex] is context - free
II. [latex]\bar{L_{1}}[/latex] is context - free
III. [latex]L_{1} - R[/latex] is context - free
IV. [latex]L_{1}\cap L_{2} [/latex] is context - free
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: CFLs are closed under union True
- II: not closed under complement False
- III: [latex]L_1-R=L_1\cap\bar R[/latex], and CFL [latex]\cap[/latex] regular is CFL True
- IV: not closed under intersection False

Answer: I and III only
